name: Multi-Repo Web Dashboard
description: Implements a lightweight web dashboard for monitoring FADE sessions across multiple repositories in real-time. Provides centralized visibility into work queues, active sessions, completed work, regression tests, and key documentation across all FADE projects.

context.problem: User runs FADE autonomously across 3-5 repositories simultaneously (fade, ai-built-actuarial-model, fade-prd-generator, assumptionsmanager, etc.). No visibility into progress when away from terminal. Must SSH into each repo separately to check status. Overnight YOLO runs are black boxes until completion. No way to monitor from phone/tablet while away.
context.realWorldScenario: User starts FADE YOLO at 01:30, goes to sleep. Wakes at 07:00 and checks progress. Currently must: (1) SSH to each machine, (2) cd to each repo, (3) run 'fade status', (4) read progress.md. Takes 15-20 minutes. Want instant overview from any device.
context.impact: Zero visibility into autonomous work means anxiety about failures, wasted time checking each repo, inability to react to issues remotely. Dashboard would provide peace of mind and faster issue detection.

solution: Create lightweight web dashboard that aggregates FADE status across repositories. Each FADE session writes status.json every 60 seconds. Central dashboard server reads these files, displays unified view. Accessible via http://localhost:8080 or remote IP. Auto-refreshes every 30 seconds for pseudo real-time updates.

userStories.title: Session status export to JSON
userStories.description: As FADE, I want to export current session state to JSON so external tools can monitor progress.
acceptanceCriteria: During FADE run/yolo, write fade/status.json every 60 seconds
JSON includes: repo name, current PRD, current story, iteration count, start time, model, mode (STOP/ALL/YOLO)
JSON includes: work queue (list of pending PRDs with story counts)
JSON includes: completed count (stories done this session)
JSON includes: last update timestamp (ISO 8601 format)
JSON includes: session status (running/blocked/complete), if blocked: reason
If session completes, write final status with completion timestamp
If session blocks, include error details from failed.log
JSON is atomic write (tmp file + rename to prevent partial reads)
Maximum 1KB file size (compress if needed)

userStories.title: Dashboard configuration and discovery
userStories.description: As a FADE user, I want to configure which repos the dashboard monitors so I see all my active projects.
acceptanceCriteria: Create ~/.fade-dashboard/config.json for dashboard settings
Config includes: list of repo paths to monitor
Config includes: dashboard port (default: 8080), refresh interval (default: 30s)
Config includes: repo display names (map path to friendly name)
Example: {'repos': [{'path': '~/Documents/GitHub/fade', 'name': 'FADE Core'}, {'path': '~/Documents/GitHub/livecalc', 'name': 'LiveCalc'}]}
Command 'fade dashboard --add /path/to/repo' updates config
Command 'fade dashboard --list' shows configured repos
Auto-discover: Scan parent directory for other FADE repos (finds FADE.md), suggest adding
Validate paths on startup, warn if repo not found

userStories.title: Dashboard server and web UI
userStories.description: As a FADE user, I want to access a web dashboard so I can monitor all repos from any device.
acceptanceCriteria: Create fade/lib/dashboard-server.py (simple Python HTTP server, no external dependencies)
Command 'fade dashboard' starts server on http://localhost:8080
Server reads all status.json files from configured repos every 30s
Server serves static HTML/CSS/JS from fade/templates/dashboard/
Dashboard shows: Repo cards with current status (running/blocked/complete)
Each card shows: Current PRD, current story, progress (X/Y stories), elapsed time, model
Each card color-coded: green (running), red (blocked), gray (idle), blue (complete)
Click repo card → expanded view with full queue, recent progress entries
Auto-refresh every 30s via JavaScript (no manual reload needed)
Mobile-friendly responsive design (works on phone/tablet)
Server runs in foreground (Ctrl+C to stop), logs requests to console
Optional: --daemon flag runs server in background, writes PID to ~/.fade-dashboard/server.pid

userStories.title: Work queue and archive visualization
userStories.description: As a FADE user, I want to see work queues and archives across repos so I understand total workload.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard aggregate view shows: Total PRDs queued across all repos
Aggregate view shows: Total stories pending, total stories completed today
Per-repo expanded view shows: PRD queue with story counts (same as 'fade status')
Per-repo expanded view shows: Archive list (completed PRDs) with completion dates
Per-repo expanded view shows: Regression test results (pass/fail counts, last run time)
Filterable view: Show only blocked repos, show only active repos
Sortable: By activity (most recent first), by workload (most stories pending)
Click PRD name → view PRD JSON (syntax highlighted)
Click archive entry → view completion summary from progress.md

userStories.title: Live documentation viewer
userStories.description: As a FADE user, I want to view key documentation files so I can review context without opening editor.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-repo view includes 'Docs' tab
Docs tab shows: FADE.md, progress.md (last 50 entries), learned.md, healing-log.md
Markdown files rendered with syntax highlighting and formatting
Click filename → view full content in modal overlay
Search within doc: Ctrl+F searches rendered content
Last modified timestamp shown for each doc
Link to raw file (opens in editor) for power users
Mobile view: Docs are scrollable, readable on small screens

userStories.title: Session history and analytics
userStories.description: As a FADE user, I want to see historical trends so I understand productivity patterns.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard aggregate view shows: Sessions run today, this week, this month
Aggregate view shows: Total stories completed (across all repos)
Aggregate view shows: Model usage breakdown (Haiku: 20%, Sonnet: 65%, Opus: 15%)
Per-repo view shows: Session timeline (last 10 sessions with duration, outcomes)
Per-repo view shows: Healing events count (auto-fixed issues)
Chart: Stories completed per day (simple ASCII bar chart or sparkline)
Chart: Session duration over time (identify trends)
Export button: Download aggregate stats as JSON for external analysis

userStories.title: Remote access and security
userStories.description: As a FADE user, I want secure remote access so I can monitor from anywhere.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard server binds to 0.0.0.0 with --remote flag (default: localhost only)
Display server URL on startup: 'Dashboard running at http://192.168.1.100:8080'
Optional basic auth: --password flag sets password, prompts on web access
HTTPS support via --cert and --key flags (self-signed cert OK for local network)
Warning if --remote used without auth: 'WARNING: Dashboard accessible to network without password'
Rate limiting: Max 100 requests/minute per IP to prevent abuse
Access log: Record all connections with IP, timestamp, endpoint
Graceful shutdown: Ctrl+C writes 'Server stopped' to log, closes connections cleanly

technicalNotes.implementation: Python 3 HTTP server (stdlib only, no pip dependencies for portability)
technicalNotes.frontend: Static HTML/CSS/vanilla JavaScript (no frameworks, fast loading)
technicalNotes.dataFlow: FADE writes status.json → Dashboard reads files → Browser polls dashboard → JavaScript updates DOM
technicalNotes.realtime: Pseudo real-time via polling (30s intervals), not WebSockets (simpler, more compatible)
technicalNotes.security: Basic auth sufficient for local network, HTTPS for internet exposure
technicalNotes.architecture: Stateless server, all state in files (FADE philosophy)
technicalNotes.performance: Minimal overhead, status.json write takes <10ms, dashboard serves <50ms response time

filesToModify.changes: Add 'fade dashboard' command, integrate status.json export into run loop (every 60s)
Call export_status_json() after each iteration to write status.json
Add dashboard section with screenshots, setup instructions, remote access guide

mustHave: FADE sessions write status.json every 60 seconds
Dashboard shows all configured repos with current status
Work queue and archive visualization per repo
niceToHave: Live documentation viewer for FADE.md, progress.md
HTTPS support for secure remote monitoring

risks.risk: Dashboard server crashes, user doesn't notice monitoring stopped
risks.mitigation: Server writes heartbeat to log. Optional systemd/launchd service for auto-restart.

risks.risk: Unsecured remote access exposes repo contents to network
risks.mitigation: Default to localhost only. Require explicit --remote flag. Warn if no auth. Recommend HTTPS for internet.

risks.risk: Frequent status.json writes impact FADE performance
risks.mitigation: Write every 60s (not every iteration). Async write in background. Max 1KB file size.

definitionOfDone: All 7 user stories have passing acceptance criteria
FADE run/yolo writes status.json every 60 seconds with current state
Dashboard server starts with 'fade dashboard', accessible at localhost:8080
Dashboard displays all configured repos with color-coded status cards
Work queue, archive, test results visible per repo
Aggregate stats across all repos shown
Documentation updated with dashboard setup and usage guide
Demo: Start FADE YOLO in 3 repos, open dashboard, see all 3 updating in real-time

setup: User has 3 repos: fade, livecalc, assumptionsmanager
Each has FADE initialized and PRDs queued
User runs: cd fade && fade yolo &
expected: Shows 3 cards: FADE Core (running), LiveCalc (running), AssumptionsManager (running)
Each card shows current PRD, story, progress, elapsed time
Cards update every 30s as work progresses
User clicks 'LiveCalc' card → sees full queue (5 PRDs, 23 stories pending)
User switches to phone → dashboard still accessible, mobile layout works
User wakes up at 7am → checks phone → sees 'FADE Core (complete), LiveCalc (blocked), AssumptionsManager (complete)'
User clicks blocked repo → sees error: 'Test failed: head: illegal line count'
User decides whether to intervene or let auto-healing handle it
